bib.title: Think Bayes, ch. 7: Prediction
bib.venue: book chapter (Think Bayes, 1st ed., Green Tea Press / O'Reilly, 2012; no journal)

question: How is a posterior over a scoring rate turned into a predictive distribution of goals, and into the probability of winning a game and a series?

results.claim: Prior over goals per game: roughly Gaussian, mean 2.8 and sd 0.3 across 2010-11 NHL teams.
results.setup: per-team average goals per game, nhl.com

results.claim: From the first four finals games the most likely lambda is 2.6 for the Canucks and 2.9 for the Bruins.
results.quote: 2.6 for the Canucks and 2.9 for the Bruins

results.claim: The goal distribution for the next game is a mixture of Poisson distributions weighted by the posterior of lambda.
results.quote: the overall distribution of goals is a mixture of these Poisson distributions

results.claim: Bruins next game: win 46%, loss 37%, tie 17% in regulation.
results.quote: p_win is 46%, p_loss is 37%, and p_tie is 17%

results.claim: Probability the Bruins win in sudden-death overtime is 52%; overall win probability for the next game is 55%.
results.setup: time to first goal exponential with rate lam, mixed over the posterior
results.quote: the overall chance of winning the next game is 55%

results.claim: The Bruins' chance of winning the series is 57% under the low-variance prior.
results.setup: win next two or split and win third
results.quote: The Bruins chance of winning the series is 57%.

results.claim: Pair-by-pair regular-season averages have mean 2.8 and sd 0.85; with that prior the series probability is 80%.
results.setup: pairs that met 4-6 times in the regular season (data from Dirk Hoag)

results.claim: The results are sensitive to the prior given how little data there is.
results.quote: the results are sensitive to the prior

limits: Text says prior mean 2.8 but the Hockey class uses 2.7; MakeGaussianPmf passes norm.pdf(mu, sigma, x) in the wrong order. Poisson process ignores variation in scoring over a game, and the prior ignores opponent quality.
practices: Model goals as a Poisson process and time between goals as exponential (p.71).
Predict with a mixture over the posterior, not a plug-in estimate (p.73).
Start simple, find the likely sources of error and iterate on the model (p.76-77).
Spend effort on the prior when data are scarce (p.77).

terms.definition: the continuous version of a Bernoulli process, where an event can occur at any point in time with equal probability
a Pmf whose values are Pmfs

lineage.note: Poisson model of scoring in a German soccer league

figures.caption: Posterior distribution of the number of goals per game.

code.snippet:
def MakeGoalPmf(suite):
    metapmf = thinkbayes.Pmf()
    for lam, prob in suite.Items():
        pmf = thinkbayes.MakePoissonPmf(lam, 10)
        metapmf.Set(pmf, prob)
    mix = thinkbayes.MakeMixture(metapmf)
    return mix
